title: Explicit-Implicit Entity Alignment Method in Multi-modal Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: MMEA aims to find equivalent entities between multi-modal knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: The embed-fuse-compare paradigm may not fully address inconsistencies across modalities, causing instability and sub-optimal performance.

contributions.claim: Introduces an embed-fuse-assign paradigm that formulates MMEA as a multi-modal assignment problem.

Proposes the EIEA algorithm, which separates modalities into explicit and implicit categories, uses modality-specific embedding and correlation scoring, and integrates correspondences across modalities.
Introduces conflict-aware soft pseudo-labeling to optimize semi-supervised learning for implicit modalities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the embed-fuse-assign paradigm and the EIEA algorithm as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the proposed paradigm and algorithm achieve state-of-the-art performance on five real-world MMEA datasets.
The authors report releasing the source code and datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines MMEA as identifying equivalent entities across multi-modal knowledge graphs.
Describes the existing embed-fuse-compare approach and its possible instability under cross-modal inconsistencies.
Reframes MMEA as a multi-modal assignment problem and identifies correspondence scoring as crucial.
Presents EIEA with explicit-implicit modality handling, modality-specific scoring, correspondence integration, and conflict-aware pseudo-labeling.
Reports state-of-the-art results on five datasets and releases source code and datasets.

source_observation.claim: EIEA classifies modalities by whether joint neighborhood information is needed and uses modality-specific mechanisms.

interpretation.claim: Different modalities may require different information dependencies and scoring mechanisms rather than uniform processing.

application.claim: When designing multi-modal systems, classify inputs by their cross-modal information needs before selecting shared or modality-specific components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the classification criteria in operational detail or identify cases where the strategy fails.

unknowns: The five datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not specified.
The assignment proof and correspondence-scoring formulation are not detailed.
The explicit/implicit modality classification criteria and model architecture are not fully described.
The pseudo-labeling procedure and ablation results are not provided.
The release contents and reproducibility conditions are not established.
